recipes.name: Irish Roast Beef with Guinness au Jus
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle Irish stout beer (e.g. Guinness®)
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place roast in a roasting pan and pour stout over top. Cover the pan with plastic wrap and marinate in the refrigerator, 8 hours to overnight, turning once.
When ready to cook, preheat the oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C).
Transfer roast to a cutting board and pat dry. Leave stout in the baking pan.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear roast for 2 to 3 minutes per side; transfer to a plate.

Crush rosemary, thyme, steak seasoning, and pepper with a mortar and pestle. Add minced garlic and stir to make a paste. Spread paste over all sides of roast. Place roast back into the roasting pan with stout, and cover loosely with foil.

Bake in the preheated oven for 2 hours. Add potatoes to the roasting pan and remove the foil. Continue to bake until an instant-read thermometer measures 145 degrees F (65 degrees C) for medium, about 1 more hour, or to desired degree of doneness. Remove from the oven, cover with a doubled sheet of aluminum foil, and allow to rest in a warm area for 20 minutes before slicing.

While the roast is resting, pour pan juices into a pot. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat and simmer until juices have reduced and thickened, about 10 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Strain and serve with beef and potatoes.

raw_recipe.headline: Irish Roast Beef with Guinness au Jus
raw_recipe.description: This Irish roast is marinated in Guinness stout, slathered with garlic and herbs, and cooked low and slow in the oven, resulting in tender, robustly flavored beef.

review.reviewBody: Made this recipe mostly as directed - only exceptions being I added the potatoes from the beginning of the oven time as well as tossed in some carrots to the mix. Smelled mouthwatering while roasting and we really enjoyed it, but I think I'll add a tad more garlic and maybe some rosemary the next time.

I made this in an electric pressure cooker. I marinated the beef for a couple of hours in 2 bottles of Guinness's. I took it out of the marinade, dried it off and slathered it with fresh ground black pepper and fresh ground sea salt (I don't use much salt) thyme, rosemary, arrow root, onion and garlic powder some whole grain mustard and some tomato paste. I put oil in the hot pot and browned all sides of the roast. I took the roast out of the pot, sautéed some scallion, celery and fresh garlic. I put in the potatoes and carrots and let them get a little color, not much really. I then put the meat and a mix of Guinness and low sodium free range organic chicken stock and a bay leaf some flour and a little brown sugar. I put the lid on and an hour later we had a VERY TENDER delicious roast, I probably didn't use enough flour as the sauce didn't thicken, but it was delicious. I think what took the longest was chopping the veggies.

I read the reviews before starting. I added tomato paste and seared the roast in Irish butter instead of olive oil. I skipped the potatoes. I thickened the gravy with Xanthan gum. This came out really good! Thanks for the recipe
Added onion to the roasting pan and garlic in the marinade. May add some A1 to the marinade next time. Needed some tang, but was still delicious!

I use this recipe to make Sheppard's Pie. I marinated over night, cut into chunks and cooked in a pressure cooker with the seasoning. When it's done I shred it, cover in mashed potatoes and Monterey Jack cheese. Fantastic every time

Mine was done in the 2 hours too. Even when I had the taters in from the start, they still weren't done, so after transferring meat and pan juices, I cranked the oven up to 350 for a bit for a beautiful crispy coating.
The roast beef was a great. My daughter who’s five mos. pregnant enjoyed eating every bite. I made minor adjustment ( seasoning, veggies, and cooked in a plastic bag) but other that is was easy.

I followed the recipe as written. It wasn't worth all the effort. We found it to lack in flavor, and the meat was tough. I wish I had tried same ingredients in the crock. Meat was done to 145 degrees in 2 hours, but potatoes and carrots were no where near done. I took the meat out, turned the oven up to 350, and finished cooking potatoes and carrots, which were good (another 30 minutes). The meal wasn't terrible, but I won't make it again. I wanted something different for a chuck roast, and this one didn't cut it.
Easy and delicious! I cooked it longer so it would be more tender.
This was an awesome roast! I didn't have Guiness so I used a bottle of Coke. Turned out fabulous.

I used a 2 lb beef roast and it was cooked perfectly to Medium in the first 2 hours. While this was a nice surprise, I wish I didn't trust the timing and checked periodically, because as it stands now, the potatoes are not cooked and I have a roast that's "getting happy" out of the oven.
My husband and I loved this recipe! I just should have used a boneless chuck roast lol It still turned out great all the same. :)
Awesome!!! Just add the potatoes when you put the roast in the oven... mine weren't cooked so I had to turn up the heat and cook longer...
I love this dish. I made for myself and my husband, we really enjoyed it. It was easy to make and it tastes amazing.
